claims.statement: The canonical verification commands are Bun scripts in package.json: `bun run check` (architecture fence + Biome + tsc --noEmit), `bun test` (frontend unit + DOM tests), `bun run check:rust` (cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets), `bun run check:worker` (ruff check, ruff format --check, stdlib unittest discover), and `bun run check:all` chaining all four; Bun is the only supported driver and `npm test` is not a valid gate.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs three parallel macos-15 jobs — frontend, rust, worker — on every push to main and every pull request, under a per-ref concurrency group that cancels superseded runs; macos-15 is chosen because the app only ships for arm64 macOS 14+ so the gates run on the platform they describe.

The CI rust job must run `bun run vite:build` before the cargo steps because tauri.conf.json points frontendDist at ../dist and the Tauri context macro fails to expand without it; vite:build itself runs tsc --noEmit first, so the job transitively re-type-checks the frontend, and Swatinem/rust-cache scopes to src-tauri.

The CI worker job runs the Python tests on a bare pinned interpreter (`uv run --python 3.12` after ruff check and ruff format --check) because every module under worker/tests imports no ML stack; keeping worker tests ML-stack-free is what keeps the CI job dependency-free.

scripts/check-architecture.ts (run as `bun run architecture:check`, first step of `bun run check`) defines eight per-layer fences forbidding literal substrings: Rust domain (crate::application, crate::adapters, crate::composition, tauri::), Rust application (crate::adapters, crate::composition, tauri::), Rust inbound/outbound adapters (cross-adapter and composition imports), and the TS mirrors (domain, application, ui, adapters) with @tauri-apps/ banned in application and ui.

check-architecture.ts performs a second framework-locality pass over all Rust source: #[tauri::command] may appear only in adapters/inbound/tauri.rs; generate_handler!, .manage(, and .plugin( only in composition.rs; tokio::process and nix:: process primitives only in adapters/outbound/process.rs and the process/ submodule directory. Violations from all passes aggregate into one ArchitectureError listing every offending file.

Because check-architecture.ts matches forbidden substrings over whole file source rather than an import graph, a forbidden token anywhere (including comments) trips the fence; the fence, not the prose documents, is the authority on where code may live, and layering changes that cannot pass it are not safe to make.

The TypeScript fences exist as a regression fence: BackendPort and related contracts originally lived in adapters/tauri-backend.ts, which forced ui/ and application/ to import an adapter module; the 2026-08 refactor moved the contracts to src/domain/backend.ts and added the TS fences (documented as violations #1 and #3 in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6).

Frontend tests are colocated with implementations as *.test.ts files (src/application/job-machine.test.ts, src/ui/app-view.dom.test.ts and peers, src/styles.test.ts) and run via `bun test`; the state machines job-machine.ts and recording-machine.ts are immutable (state, event) → state reducers tested as pure functions with no DOM or IPC.

DOM test suites import Window from happy-dom, construct the real AppView over a real DOM element, and inject the real styles.css as a stylesheet so selectors, hidden flags, data-state, and aria-current are exercised against actual markup; recording-controller.dom.test.ts additionally installs the happy-dom window/document onto globalThis because the controller drives window.setInterval and the visibility listener directly.

Frontend reducer tests pin externally observable contract behaviors: progress never moves backwards within a phase, the diagnostic log stays bounded at 200 entries, events from a stale job id return the same state object, a cancelled job stays cancelled when the dying worker later reports an error, and recording elapsed time follows wall clock (single tick after a background minute shows 60 seconds) and is monotonic against backwards clock steps.

src/styles.test.ts pins stylesheet invariants — `html [hidden]` keeps display:none and the workspace grid reserves four row tracks so the #app-error banner keeps its row (regression VQA-006) — because DOM text/hidden assertions once passed while a grid-row collapse visually hid the banner; DOM visibility checks are not pixel visibility.

src-tauri/src/application/tests.rs is the main Rust use-case suite: a single FakePort implements every port Application consumes (engine, transcription, import, artifacts, recording, settings, refinement) over shared Mutex/atomic state that records observations, with a switchable TranscriptionBehavior (Success, Failure, Blocking) where Blocking signals the job started via mpsc and then awaits cancellation.

The application suite pins guard ordering and lifecycle rules: an invalid speaker hint is rejected with INVALID_SPEAKER_HINT before any workspace access (prepare_calls == 0); refinement without a saved key fails with ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING; cancellation reaches a running port without timing waits and returns CANCELLED; a failed transcription releases the active job slot so a retry succeeds.

The application suite pins roster/glossary propagation: saved participants, aliases, and glossary terms travel into the ASR biasing context and onto each refinement job (selected attendees travel in roster order, the glossary travels whole on every refinement), and no ASR context is sent when nothing is saved.

src-tauri/src/application/tests/recording.rs pins the recording lifecycle at the use-case level: re-entry is refused with RECORDING_BUSY, stopping a wrong session id fails with RECORDING_ID_MISMATCH, and stop/cancel round-trip through the started recording id.

Rust fakes follow the LSP rule from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4: a FakePort must preserve the production contract (stable error codes, event ordering), and when production evolves and a fake drifts, the fake is fixed to match production — never production weakened to match the fake.

adapters/outbound/process/tests.rs pins the worker-supervisor contract: a line over MAX_LINE_BYTES is rejected before unbounded growth (WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR), a `refined` stdout event is captured as the process result, cancelling a running child returns CANCELLED promptly and reaps it, and a failing child reports its last stderr line rather than its first.

Domain-level Rust tests pin the cross-language worker protocol at the host end: domain/worker.rs tests cover parsing phase events at protocol v1, rejecting newer versions and malformed JSON, and AsrContext serializing to exactly the keys the worker's parse_asr_context reads; application/jobs.rs tests pin the registry (one job at a time with BUSY, the slot frees when the guard drops, double-cancel reports ALREADY_CANCELLING, unknown ids report JOB_NOT_FOUND).

adapters/outbound/paths/tests.rs pins output-layout behavior: meeting folders are named after the recording, a recording's own folder is reused, colliding folder names deduplicate (meeting 2), and a new job is seeded with the latest matching checkpoint from a previous run even across different folder names.

Recording adapter tests pin sample conversion and WAV output: float samples are clamped at i16 bounds with NaN/infinity mapped to 0, a Core Audio xrun is treated as a recoverable stream error, the WAV writer produces byte-exact PCM with the expected header, and dropped samples are filled with silence and reported in the summary; the SleepBlocker pmset test is #[ignore]d for sandboxed CI and runs with `cargo test -- --ignored` on a real desktop.

Worker tests use only the standard library with package-relative imports (`from ..galpi_worker...`) resolved by `unittest discover -s worker/tests -t .`, and cover only pure modules (core, qwen3, artifacts, preparation, protocol, runtime, minutes_prompt, minutes_pipeline, assistant_stream, and the CLI parser) that import no ML stack — heavy ML imports stay lazy inside runtime functions, making the purity boundary the worker's tested edge.

Two worker test files are shared case libraries, not discoverable modules: minutes_prompt_cases.py and refine_stream_cases.py define unittest.TestCase classes that test_core.py re-exports through __all__, so `unittest discover` (which only picks up test*.py files) executes them through test_core.

Worker tests pin protocol integrity and progress semantics: an EventWriter JSONL stream stays isolated from dependency stdout noise (a print under redirect_stdout never reaches the protocol stream), the download reporter maps downloaded bytes onto the models phase band, throttles to prevent flooding, and reports nothing before a size is known.

Worker tests pin hallucination-filter thresholds: a segment is flagged at six dominant repeated tokens but kept at five, natural speech reusing common fillers is preserved, and ASR hotwords respect the char budget by dropping whole entries rather than cutting mid-word.

Worker tests pin the Qwen3 pipeline invariants: audio chunks never exceed the 30-second runtime resplit limit, sentence grouping keeps model text verbatim while chunks only time it, splitting occurs at speaker turns and long pauses with boundary words assigned to the nearest speaker, and the bias context is capped so it cannot crowd out the audio.

Worker tests pin long-meeting routing and the CLI contract: transcripts split only at whole speaker-turn boundaries with oversized turns kept whole, each chunk after the first carries the previous tail as explicitly context-only preamble with sequential chunk numbering, and the transcribe/prepare CLI accepts qwen3/whisperx engine flags while rejecting unknown engines.

Biome lints all TypeScript with noExplicitAny, noDefaultExport, useImportType, and unused variables/imports at error; tsc runs strict with exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, and verbatimModuleSyntax both in `bun run check` and in every `bun run vite:build`.

clippy is enforced twice: the crate itself denies unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, todo, and unimplemented with pedantic at warn (Cargo.toml [lints.clippy]), and CI adds `-D warnings` so any warning fails the rust job; basedpyright runs strict over worker/ with local stubs (pyrightconfig.json stubPath worker/stubs) but needs a WhisperX-enabled interpreter (`uvx basedpyright --pythonpath <WhisperX Python>`), so it is documented as a full-verification command rather than a CI step — both clippy and basedpyright are treated as release gates.

The tag-triggered release workflow builds and uploads the DMG (optionally signing/notarizing with conditional codesign/spctl verification) but runs none of the check gates — verification is CI's job, the release workflow only packages.

New external capabilities arrive as one change set: declare the trait in src-tauri/src/application/ports.rs, implement it in an outbound adapter, wire it in composition.rs, and extend FakePort in application/tests.rs — a port without a fake is an incomplete change.

Worker protocol, event, and field changes move as one commit set across worker/galpi_worker/protocol.py, src-tauri/src/domain/worker.rs, src/domain/job.ts (with the Zod schemas in src/adapters/tauri-backend.ts), and src/application/job-machine.ts, with the parser tests on both ends moving alongside; new UI state gets a reducer in src/application/*-machine.ts with a colocated test while the view only renders.

Test quality rules: verify observable behavior through public contracts (port methods, view selectors, reducer outputs) not implementation details; keep tests deterministic with no wall-clock, sleeps, real network, or ordering dependence; one behavior per test; never weaken production behavior (e.g. loosening a Zod schema) to pass; and prefer the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior while preserving complete failure output.
Behavioral tests across all three runtimes use // Given / // When / // Then comments where setup is nontrivial (e.g. process/tests.rs, application/tests.rs, job-machine.test.ts, test_core.py).

The project's verification-gate commands, test-structure conventions, and test-quality rules live in `.issueops/testing/overview.md`, whose canonical index is `.issueops/TESTING.md` (the family root that links the focused testing module).
